scope.boundary_rule: Manual recovery of the missed scheduled noon run. Only evidence publicly available by 12:00 ET is admitted; later Sep.30 reporting belongs to the next window.

recovery_context.reason: The noon automation did not execute because the standing Atlas Evidence Sweep task was disabled. The task has been restored to its original 00:00/12:00 ET schedule and this artifact backfills the missed 12:00 ET horizon.

new_events.summary: EASA issued an advisory urging covered operators to avoid Saudi Arabian airspace amid increased Houthi attacks, upgraded Jordan to an all-altitude avoidance recommendation, and extended warnings covering Lebanon, Iran, Iraq and territorial Gulf waters of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and Oman through November 16.

existing_event_updates.summary: Reuters reported that Qatari mediators relayed U.S. feedback to Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Iran's seven-day trust-building plan. A non-Iranian official briefed on the talks said the main disagreement concerned sequencing rather than the components of the plan. This establishes continuing mediated bargaining after Trump's public rejection, not U.S. acceptance or a new agreement.

Reuters reported that shipping through Hormuz had increased in recent weeks but crude, refined-product and gas flows remained substantially disrupted, while UKMTO continued to report projectile incidents. This does not establish normalization and does not replace denominator-compatible Kpler/LSEG traffic series.

economic_energy_updates.summary: Reuters' intraday energy update reported Goldman Sachs estimated Gulf oil exports at 23.3 million barrels per day over the prior week, in line with the 2025 average, while JPMorgan estimated the five-day 10-day-average total oil-export rate at 20.5 million bpd, about 89% of 2025 levels. Brent and WTI were higher at the 10:50 ET market snapshot. These are bank/market estimates and do not establish full Hormuz traffic normalization.
